styleWhy: It is an event with a date, a culprit and a money trail, so telling it as breaking news (the banner, a running clock, the trail, the FBI's words) carries the story and its tension.

copy.idea: On 21 February 2025, about $1.5 billion in crypto was stolen from the exchange Bybit, the biggest crypto theft on record. The video follows the money: out of a cold wallet, split across thousands of addresses, swapped into bitcoin, and the FBI naming North Korea five days later.
copy.hook: About $1.5 billion in crypto was taken from the exchange Bybit in a single hack on 21 February 2025.
copy.body:
Roughly 401,000 ETH left one of Bybit's cold wallets, the offline storage exchanges treat as the safest place they have.

No crypto theft before it came close: the previous records, Ronin Network and Poly Network, were around $600 million each.

The thieves moved fast. The funds were split across thousands of addresses on several blockchains and much of it was swapped into bitcoin, which makes it harder to follow.

Five days later, the FBI said North Korea was responsible, naming the group it calls TraderTraitor.

facts.text: “North Korea Responsible for $1.5 Billion Bybit Hack”; “the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of approximately $1.5 billion in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit on or about February 21, 2025.”
facts.source: FBI Public Service Announcement I-022625-PSA, 26 Feb 2025 — https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226

facts.text: “TraderTraitor actors are proceeding rapidly and have converted some of the stolen assets to Bitcoin and other virtual assets dispersed across thousands of addresses on multiple blockchains.”
facts.source: FBI Public Service Announcement I-022625-PSA, 26 Feb 2025 — https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226

facts.text: About 401,000 ETH (plus smaller amounts of staked ETH tokens), worth about $1.46 billion, was taken from a Bybit Ethereum cold wallet; the largest crypto theft on record.
facts.source: Elliptic, 'Bybit hack largest in history', 21 Feb 2025 — https://www.elliptic.co/blog/bybit-hack-largest-in-history

facts.text: Earlier record thefts: Ronin Network, about $625 million (March 2022); Poly Network, about $611 million (August 2021), values as reported at the time.
facts.source: Elliptic, 'Bybit hack largest in history', 21 Feb 2025 — https://www.elliptic.co/blog/bybit-hack-largest-in-history

facts.text: Illustrative, not sourced: the transaction rows, their hashes and times, the shape of the money trail and the mixer are drawn to show how laundering works, not the real transfers.

shots.title: Hook: breaking, $1.5B gone
shots.show: A LIVE chip with '21 FEB 2025' and a BREAKING banner wipe in at the top: 'Crypto exchange Bybit hacked'. Below, a huge red counter rolls up to $1.5B and slams down with a red alarm flash and a shake; 'stolen in a single hack' lands under it, a hooded hacker icon below; behind, a rain of ETH coins falls past.
shots.motion: On the voice: the banner wipes in with "Breaking", the counter rolls from 0 and lands on "dollars" with the flash and shake, the line lands on "single hack"; coins keep falling until the cut.
shots.say: Breaking: 1.5 billion dollars in crypto, gone in a single hack.

shots.title: The cold wallet drains
shots.show: The Bybit cold wallet card (recurring) sits at the top; one transfer empties it, its balance dropping to 0 and its border pulsing red; under it, outgoing transfer rows (illustrative hashes) keep landing, the big ones flagged red, scrolling past.
shots.motion: The balance drops to 0 on "emptied" with an alarm flash; rows land every 0.22 s from then and scroll; the headline number types in on "401,000".
shots.say: One transfer emptied Bybit's cold wallet. About 401,000 ether, on the move.

shots.title: The biggest ever
shots.show: A bar race of the biggest crypto thefts: Poly Network 2021 ($611M) and Ronin 2022 ($625M) grow first in gray, then Bybit 2025 shoots past both and the old record's dashed line in red to $1.46B; a yellow NEW RECORD stamp lands.
shots.motion: Gray bars grow first; Bybit's bar shoots up on "biggest" with a counter on top; the stamp lands with a flash and shake just after "old record".
shots.source: Elliptic, 21 Feb 2025 · values as reported at the time · 1.46 ÷ 0.625 ≈ 2.3
shots.say: That makes it the biggest crypto theft ever, more than twice the old record.

shots.title: Split, swapped into bitcoin
shots.show: The money trail: one red-bordered node (the cold wallet) at the top splits into 4, then 16, then 64 wallets, ETH coins running down the branches; the last row dims as it 'goes dark'. Below, the coins pour into a mixer vortex: they swirl in ETH blue and leave bitcoin orange. Labels: 'thousands of addresses' beside the bottom row, 'swapped to bitcoin' beside the mixer.
shots.motion: Branches draw on level by level from "split", coins running along them; "thousands of addresses" lands with its words; the mixer turns from "swapped", the BTC icon pops on "bitcoin" and the last row dims.
shots.source: FBI PSA I-022625-PSA, 26 Feb 2025 · trail illustrative
shots.say: The thieves split it across thousands of addresses, and swapped some of it into bitcoin.

shots.title: FBI names North Korea
shots.show: A dark map zooms into the Korean peninsula; an FBI shield badge pops in, then the announcement's headline is typed in as a quote with its date under it; North Korea lights red and an ATTRIBUTED stamp lands.
shots.motion: Map zooms in until "North Korea"; the badge pops on "FBI" and the quote types in after it; on "North Korea" the country lights red and the stamp lands with a flash and shake.
shots.say: Five days later, the FBI said who was behind it: North Korea.

shots.title: End card: the timeline
shots.show: A vertical timeline: 21 Feb 2025, '$1.5B drained from Bybit' (glowing red), then 26 Feb 2025, 'FBI: North Korea did it'; between them a clock and the gap counting up to 5 days; a news ticker crawls under it with the three facts.
shots.motion: The axis draws down, the events land in turn; on "five days" the gap counts 0 to 5; the ticker crawls the whole time.
shots.source: FBI PSA I-022625-PSA, 26 Feb 2025 · Elliptic, 21 Feb 2025
shots.say: From hack to attribution: five days.

recurring.name: Bybit cold wallet
recurring.design: A wallet card with the ETH coin on the left, 'Bybit cold wallet' over its balance; red border once it is drained. In shot 4 it is the red-bordered top node of the trail.
